nodes.description: Immutable constant address 0x4f2CCc35F791e763779f711168424b766Ba3468F of the LeviathanWhirlpool contract whose release() is invoked and whose info is queried.
Immutable constant address 0x999b1e6EDCb412b59ECF0C5e14c20948Ce81F40b of the Whirlpool contract queried via getAllInfoFor.
External view function check(uint _requirement) that reads whirlpool data and returns the missing amount.
External function execute() that performs an unchecked external call to IRelease.release() on the LeviathanWhirlpool address.
Parameter _requirement of check(), the threshold compared against userData[10].
Local uint256[12] memory userData returned by IWhirlpool.getAllInfoFor for the LeviathanWhirlpool address.
External call IWhirlpool(_whirlpool).getAllInfoFor(_leviathanWhirlpool) returning data from an external contract, returning values are not validated.
External call IRelease(_leviathanWhirlpool).release() executed without access control or reentrancy protection.
Arithmetic operation _requirement - userData[10] compiled with Solidity <=0.6.2, i.e. without built-in overflow/underflow checks.

edges.reason: check() takes _requirement as its input parameter.
check() declares and holds the local array userData.
_whirlpool state variable supplies the target address for the getAllInfoFor external call.
_leviathanWhirlpool state variable is passed as the queried user argument to getAllInfoFor.
check() invokes the external getAllInfoFor call.
Return value of getAllInfoFor is assigned to local userData.
userData[10] flows into the unchecked subtraction.
_requirement flows into the unchecked subtraction _requirement - userData[10].
check() executes the subtraction in the else branch when userData[10] < _requirement.
_leviathanWhirlpool address is the target of the external release() call.
execute() performs the external IRelease.release() call with no reentrancy guard or access control.
The external release() call can re-enter execute() since no state guard or access restriction prevents it.

normalization_plan.reason: Non-core parameter _requirement has no standalone security meaning; it is only relevant as an operand of the unchecked subtraction unsafe operation.
Non-core local array userData exists solely to store the result of the external getAllInfoFor unsafe operation.
